cues.text: Good morning everyone. Well, in today’s tutorial we’re going to discuss the essays that you have to submit by the end of next week.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Some of you will have already started them, which is good and if you haven’t, well that’s OK but you’ll have to get a move on.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: So, let’s begin with you Simon. What’s happening with you?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, I’ve made a start on it.  I’ve research the background quite extensively last weekend and I should get to the writing tomorrow with a
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: What are you writing about?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I decided to look at the car manufacturing company, Jaguar, examine the problems they had with Q22 reliability in the 1970s and 80s, how they dealt with it, and how it affected their marketing and sales strategy.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: That sounds pretty interesting. Any problems with that?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: At the start I had problems getting information from that far back, but after rooting around in the library,
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: I found some magazines which gave me information and also gave me references to find other stuff.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: It seems now the only problem is keeping to the 4,000 word limit.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: It just seems that I have so much to write about. It seems I’ll need 5000 or even 6000 words to be able to cope.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: Yes, your essay title seems to me to be very wide-ranging.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Would you think about cutting out part of it?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: How about looking at their sales and marketing strategy but only mentioning the problems in the 70s and 80s and not going too far into it?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: That’s a good idea. That will make it much easier to handle.
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: By the way, how do you want us to hand in our work? Do you want us to drop in a hard copy to your office?
cues.speaker: Simon

cues.text: You could do that but I’d prefer it if you just e-mailed it to me as an attachment.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: You’ve all got my address. If not, give it to the secretary clearly marked that it’s for me. Right, Jennifer, how about you?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I’ve not really got going on it yet but I’ve decided on a subject.
cues.speaker: Jennifer

cues.text: I’ll try and do some research during the rest of this week and I should get writing this weekend.
cues.speaker: Jennifer

cues.text: OK, what are you writing about then
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I want to look into how supermarkets market surveys to develop use their products.
cues.speaker: Jennifer

cues.text: Will you have enough time to find out what sort of things that the supermarkets do? You won’t have much time for that.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I should be OK. I’ve had a look in the stack system in the library and I’ve found a magazine that surveyed all the UK major supermarkets and a trade publication that analysed the same things in Canadian supermarkets.
cues.speaker: Jennifer

cues.text: Be careful about using their conclusions too much. The university takes a tough stance on plagiarism .
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Make sure you properly list where you get your information from in a bibliography and try and do your own analysis. Get going too as that analysis will take a bit of time.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: OK, thanks.
cues.speaker: Jennifer

cues.text: And Melanie. How is your work going?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I’m a bit behind I’m afraid. I was sick all last week and weekend with flu.
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: I’ve got a subject I think but I’ve not done any work on it yet. Is there any chance I can get an extension to the submittal date?
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: The policy of the department is not to give any extensions unless there are extenuating circumstances. Do you have a doctor’s certificate or anything?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I went to the doctor’s but I didn’t get a note as I didn’t realise I would need it.
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: The doctor will have a record of me though as I got a prescription. I’ll go back and get one.
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: Yes, do. If you get one, then there shouldn’t be a problem getting an extension.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Without it though, you’ll be in trouble. What subject are you considering anyway?
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: I thought I’d do an overview of  the UK mortgage interest rates and their effect on housing sales trends over the last 10 years.
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: I thought it might be of interest because of the huge increases of house prices over the last decade.
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: Certainly an interesting subject and it should be no great problem getting information as this has been fairly well documented.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: It’s a lot of work again though and you’ll really need to get cracking on it even with the extension – if you get one.
cues.speaker: Tutor

cues.text: Well, I’ve not got much on for the rest of the week and I’ve set aside the weekend to really get to grips with it.
cues.speaker: Melanie

cues.text: Good. Now, is there anything else
cues.speaker: Tutor
